definition-changed.answer: §2002:4 (4.166) 'One or more runtime modules that interact with one another and that function, at execution time, as an entity' and §2023:3.158 (which adds only 'independent') name the same entity, so 'the first reference to this function in the run unit' covers the same references. The 2023 witness l1_random_unseeded_first_reference runs clean at --std 2002 (the reader's probe), so the scope and evidence do not change.

pending-clause.answer: §2002:8.8.1.1 to 8.8.1.3.6 govern the evaluation of arithmetic expressions (§2002:8.8.1.1 'The following rules apply regardless of the mode of arithmetic that is in effect'), and 15/15.1 the kinds of function; AR4 does no arithmetic and its only subject is the seed when argument-1 is absent, so the 32-digit standard arithmetic (PB5575) cannot change what it governs. §2002:15.1 item 4 ('A numeric function has an operational sign') says what 2023 15.2 says for a numeric function. 14.5.2.1.2.1 (initial state of data), 14.5.3 (transfers of control) and 14.5.10 (normal termination: files, ALLOCATE storage, objects, locale) say nothing about the RANDOM sequence. The rule rests on its own words and the run-unit definition only.
